correctness.rationale: The headline is a rigorous impossibility proof, not an experimental claim. Verified step-by-step: (1) Expansion L^6 = sum 6!/alpha! a^alpha x^alpha is multinomial theorem, correct. (2) Apolar rule x^alpha o X^beta = beta!/(beta-alpha)! X^{beta-alpha} gives x^alpha o F = alpha! c_alpha for |alpha|=6, correct. (3) Hence L^6 o F = 720 F(a) (*) holds exactly; independently re-executed in sympy-free integer arithmetic for Fermat and Perazzo-like sextics (2880=720*4, 5760=720*8). (4) k algebraically closed char 0 => k infinite, F!=0 => exists a with F(a)!=0; 720!=0 => [L^6]!=0 in 1-dim socle A_6. (5) Thus (xL)^6!=0 as A_0->A_6 while (xL)^7=0 since A_7=0, so nilpotency index exactly 7 and largest Jordan block exactly 7. (6) Nonvanishing locus {F(a)!=0} is complement of sextic hypersurface in P^3, hence nonempty Zariski open: holds for general L. This directly contradicts the target conjunction clause 'longest part at most 6'. Boundary conditions explicit: needs char not dividing 720 (char 0 assumed) and k infinite; both satisfied by target hypothesis. Conjugate arithmetic (7,5,5,5,3,3,1,1) sum 30 independently recomputed. Computation artifacts are corroboration only; proof does not depend on them. No gap, no hidden genericity confusion.
